research_header.return_basis: Nominal INR before personal taxes; execution costs separate sensitivity

gates.reason: No substantiated severe minority abuse, but recurring bank-reporting gaps, material related-party sales and a pending related-party merger need scrutiny.
gates.resolution: Reconcile recurring bank returns; assess final merger allocation, actual related-party collections and minority outcome.

gates.reason: Audited accounts and cash reconcile; stock bank-return difference has an explicit valuation-basis explanation. Missing submissions and recurrent note weaknesses remain material monitoring items, not demonstrated book-asset misstatement.
gates.resolution: Obtain corrected bank-basis reconciliation or subsequent audited closure; quantify MSMED interest and remaining confirmations. Lender private acknowledgement is not an absolute prerequisite.

gates.reason: Audited liquidity plus documented facilities and conservative dated base funding support financeability, conditional on CC renewal, collateral eligibility and modeled collection. Stress paths are not funded.
gates.resolution: Verify renewal after 25 February 2027, actual Euro/EMI balances, ≤90-day receivable eligibility, machine settlement and post-expansion cash conversion.

gates.reason: New-purchase implementation cannot be supported with incomplete full-window trading/no-trade status, unknown spreads/restrictions and material whole-lot constraints.
gates.resolution: Verify current exchange restrictions, executable bid/ask and position-specific full-window liquidity before any implementation assessment.

factors.definition: Governance, minority protection and capital-allocation stewardship.
material_facts: Complete FY2026 main, CARO and IFC reports do not identify fraud, default, diversion or ineffective internal financial controls; the auditor resignation annexure explicitly denies information obstruction.
Bank-return failures recur across FY2024 and FY2026. The pending related-party tooling-company merger expands shares 30%, and FY2026 related-party sales are 7.55% of revenue.
factors.contrary_fact: The stock valuation difference has a plausible cost-versus-selling-price explanation; a disclosed related-party transaction or auditor transition is not proof of misconduct.
factors.rationale: Adequate conduct with material explainable control and allocation concerns, not a proven-abuse score. No higher stewardship rating until reconciliations and merger outcomes are evidenced.

factors.definition: Contestability and durability of excess manufacturing economics.
material_facts: Customer qualification, tooling/process integration and quality systems support recurring engineering-component supply.
Historical top 10 customers account for 77.14% of revenue; customer-approved inputs and short orders limit bargaining power.
factors.contrary_fact: Process qualification creates friction against replacement, but competitors offer similar moulding capabilities and no unique owned IP or enduring price premium is established.
factors.rationale: Useful but contestable relationships and process capability. ISO/IATF certification is a qualification standard, not by itself a structural moat.

factors.definition: Demonstrated underlying revenue growth, not the size of an addressable market.
material_facts: Preferred FY2021–FY2026 revenue CAGR is 41.20%; FY2023–FY2026 cross-check is 53.16%.
Standalone operations grew organically with new licensed capacity. Excluding disclosed related-party goods sales, FY2026 revenue still grew 64.80%.
factors.contrary_fact: FY2021 is a pandemic-affected base; actual production, selling-price and customer-program growth splits are unavailable. Related-party revenue increased substantially.
factors.rationale: Reported CAGR earns raw 9, reduced only by the Medium-confidence ceiling of 8. No size/order-book bonus or discretionary modifier; economic capacity and recurring EBITDA corroborate substantial real growth.

factors.definition: Accessible demand and reinvestment runway, excluding capital-return quality.
material_facts: Electrical controls, industrial, automotive and emerging healthcare/childcare/precast programs offer several accessible end markets.
Seven commissioned machines in June 2026 and dated electrical-component orders demonstrate capacity and customer access beyond a generic TAM.
factors.contrary_fact: Current concentration, committed long-term quantities, new-machine utilization and program margins are not quantified; recurring OEM orders are not an irrevocable backlog.
factors.rationale: A credible expansion runway exists, but customer dependence, procurement cycles and unseasoned capacity constrain durability confidence.

factors.definition: Attributable incremental NOPAT relative to additional invested capital.
material_facts: FY2023–FY2026 adjusted corporate capital increases ₹29.7695 cr while normalized NOPAT increases ₹6.1486 cr:20.65% incremental return.
A₹.914 cr annual old-depreciation proxy lowers the estimate to 18.35%; adding ₹4 cr lease-capital sensitivity lowers it further to 16.18%, against an analyst 12–16% cost-of-capital range.
factors.contrary_fact: No plant/customer cohort attribution is disclosed, rental capacity makes capital comparability imperfect, and June 2026 assets have not produced FY2026 audited earnings.
factors.rationale: Adequate, potentially attractive incremental economics, not proven durable large excess returns. The bridge supports scoring rather than requiring unavailable private cohorts, while uncertainty prevents 7–8.

factors.definition: Operating cash realization and working-capital discipline.
material_facts: FY2024–FY2026 CFO/PAT is 0.3613 x, or 0.4222 x after removing the FY2025 depreciation reversal at 25% tax; cash capex exceeds CFO in each year.
Core trade working capital/sales is 23.44%,24.32%,24.34% in FY2024–FY2026, not a recent declining intensity; FY2026 deposits absorb a further ₹.6098 cr.
factors.contrary_fact: CFO remains positive; FY2026 receivable days improve to 73 and 98.99% of receivables are under six months. Real growth explains some absorption but does not establish full collection or prove the weakness transient.
factors.rationale: Weak realized conversion merits 4. Persistent poor cash realization alone can justify≤3 under the framework. Here positive cash generation, predominantly young receivables and evidenced growth absorption support a borderline 4 rather than 3; this is a judgment, not proof that weakness is temporary. Monitoring remains demanding.

factors.definition: Funding resilience, claims and access to liquidity.
material_facts: FY2026 gross debt ₹10.859 cr, cash ₹3.0115 cr and net debt/EBITDA0.64 x are manageable on audited earnings.

Disclosed facilities include ₹13 cr CC and ₹3.15 cr machinery finance. The conservative base waterfall funds essential uses without equity rescue under explicit renewal and eligible-collateral assumptions.
factors.contrary_fact: CC is on-demand/12-month, only≤90-day receivables and paid stock qualify, Euro debt floats, and linked bear/high-growth cases breach the cash floor.
factors.rationale: Manageable base case with meaningful stress sensitivity. Neither the aggregate ₹22.10 cr facility nor all stated cash is treated as unconditional spare liquidity.

factors.definition: Delivery of operating commitments and adaptation.
material_facts: FY2024–FY2026 revenue expands ₹25.29 cr to ₹74.38 cr and recurring EBITDA₹4.28 cr to ₹12.29 cr, corroborating delivered scaling rather than only announcements.
June 2026 machinery commissioning is disclosed with models and cost; IPO working-capital use is reported as deployed.
factors.contrary_fact: Current machine utilization, program-level returns and order completion cash receipts are unavailable; merger and JV milestones remain incomplete at the cutoff.
factors.rationale: Demonstrated expansion with incomplete milestone-to-cash evidence. Not enough repeated, fully measured execution cycles for a high score.

factors.definition: Recurring operating sources of profit growth and per-share outcomes.
material_facts: FY2026 normalized PAT excluding other income at 25% tax is ₹7.2678 cr, versus ₹3.8094 cr for FY2025; EBITDA margins 15.32%→16.52% support recurring operating improvement.
FY2025 reported PAT includes a ₹3.193 cr retrospective depreciation reversal; current depreciation also falls ₹.914 cr versus the previous method.
factors.contrary_fact: FY2026 normalized earnings growth is real, but approved options and the pending share-swap can dilute per-share claims; target-company FD income must not become a manufacturing margin.
factors.rationale: Mixed comparability and prospective dilution prevent a high earnings-quality score despite strong normalized operating progress.

factors.definition: Supported base-case annualized return relative to the 15% nominal pretax equity hurdle.
material_facts: The base case at the 16 October historical ₹394.45 quote produces 13.32% dated five-year IRR under stated funding assumptions.
The resulting spread is-1.68 percentage points; the framework−2 to<0 band is 5.
factors.contrary_fact: The quote is historical, execution costs are not observed and funding depends on renewals/collateral eligibility. Bear and bull paths with cash-floor breaches have no ordinary IRR.
factors.rationale: Current-price factor NS because no authenticated cutoff-session quote. Historical-reference scenario assessment follows: Mechanically derived from the supported conditional base model, not an additional qualitative haircut.

factors.definition: Downside severity and survival under linked operating and financing stress.
material_facts: The bear case combines 7% growth,12% EBITDA margin,30% working capital/sales and 8 x exit; its first cash-floor breach is 2027-03-31.
Full CC nonrenewal repayment on 25 February 2027 also breaches the funding floor. Hypothetical rescue is separately priced at 35% discount plus 5% fees.
factors.contrary_fact: Audited leverage is moderate, cash generation remains positive and sanctioned facilities support the base case; modeled cash-floor breaches are not evidence of an actual default.
factors.rationale: Material impairment and recapitalization risk under credible linked stress. Terminal prices on unfunded paths are illustrations, not reliable realizable recoveries.

factors.definition: Demandingness and robustness of price-implied assumptions.
material_facts: Base 18% growth,16.5% EBITDA margin and 10 x exit do not reach the 15% hurdle at ₹394.45; the conditional 15% maximum price is ₹366.81.
A12% hurdle has a funded reverse-growth root, while 15% and 18% have no funded crossing in the tested growth range at unchanged base margin/capital intensity.
factors.contrary_fact: The base growth is far below recent history, but extrapolating historical growth requires more working capital and capex; it is not a free valuation cure.
factors.rationale: Current-price factor NS because no authenticated cutoff-session quote. Historical-reference scenario assessment follows: Limited room for execution, funding or multiple errors. Separate from R: this factor assesses assumption robustness rather than return level alone.

factors.definition: Practical execution and exit for the illustrative ₹500,000 reference position.
material_facts: Only 43 issuer rows appear in 60 validated exchange-session archives and 15 in 20; missing rows cannot be declared zero-trade sessions.
The current lot is 500 shares. Observed median 1500 shares/day gives zero whole-lot capacity at 2%,5% or 10% participation.
factors.contrary_fact: Actual trading exists, including 1000 shares on 16 October, but spreads, complete surveillance status and the full-window no-trade denominator are not verified.
factors.confidence: Low for execution; High for retained historical rows
factors.rationale: NS, not an invented low or neutral point score. G4 holds new-purchase implementation; IAS remains incomplete.

GQS.ranking_caveat: Conditional governance/reliability/funding gates; G4 implementation hold does not invalidate historical operating-quality comparison.

IAS.ranking_caveat: Current R/P andL areNS; historical16October R5/P4 diagnostics are separate. G4 holds implementation. No midpoint or renormalization.

CASH_minus1.override_condition: A move to3 supported by persistent poor cash realization invokes framework cap; not automatically applied to a purely statistical score perturbation.

classification.final: Hold — unresolved for implementation; mixed-quality growth research watchlist
classification.quality_ranking_conditions: G1/G2/G3 Conditional, no demonstrated severe failure; G4 implementation hold does not invalidate audited historical quality comparison.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
paragraphs: Master Components is a genuine small engineering-plastics manufacturer with rapid organic scaling, not merely an announced capacity story. Recurring EBITDA has grown with sales, and an adjusted three-year capital bridge suggests adequate incremental returns. Those strengths coexist with weak earnings-to-cash realization, customer bargaining power, recurring bank-reporting weaknesses and unsettled dilution.

BQS 5.6/10 and GQS 6.6/10 describe mixed business quality and comparatively stronger growth. IAS is NS, not a buy ranking: current R/P and liquidity cannot be fully scored and G4 holds implementation. Historical 16 October scenario scores R5/P4 remain diagnostics only. GOV5 reflects explainable concerns without an evidenced-abuse allegation. No governance/funding numeric override is triggered.

At the last verified actual ₹394.45 trade on 16 October 2026, the conditional base earns 13.32% before personal tax and execution costs, below the 15% hurdle. Its hurdle-compatible price is ₹366.81, conditional on all modeled operating and financing assumptions, not an executable bid or universal fair value. Bear and rapid-growth cases breach cash floors; their ordinary returns and entry prices are NULL.

Classification: Hold — unresolved for new-purchase implementation; research watchlist with mixed quality, strong recent growth and material cash/funding sensitivities. Not an evidence-backed compounder candidate. No portfolio allocation or trade instruction is implied.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
paragraphs: Legal entity: Master Components Limited; CIN L28900MH1999PLC123308; NSE Emerge MASTER; ISIN INE0OJM01017. Incorporated 27 December 1999, public conversion 4 January 2023 and listed 29 September 2023. The FY2026 corporate page omits the O in the ISIN; the dated exchange master and earlier records resolve that typographical conflict. This is a standalone manufacturer, not the similarly named tooling transferor Master Moulds Private Limited.

Information cutoff 20 October 2026; retrieval and preparation 22 October 2026. Audited period 31 March 2026, report filed 7 June 2026, audit 15 May 2026. Dated market reference window ends 19 October; the last retained issuer trade is 16 October. No 19 October issuer row was found, so no false 19 October closing quote is asserted.

Framework v 3.0, full research mode, SME batch 241–260. Currency ₹crore unless marked lakh/rupees/yen. Five-year investor dates 19 October 2026–19 October 2031,1826 days/365.25. Hurdle 15% nominal INR pretax, sensitivity 12%/18%; illustrative reference position ₹500,000 is not personalized suitability advice.

Historical financial/source confidence is Medium to High; incremental attribution and forecasts are Medium; execution confidence is Low. Primary annual reports, complete statutory annexures, dated exchange archives and material filings dominate. Recent credit-rating confirmation and complete current surveillance/spread evidence were not located. Gates below are assessments, not guarantees.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
paragraphs: Each factor is assigned once and reused exactly. BQS and GQS are not blended. IAS uses unrounded BQS; numeric strings and Decimal contributions preserve arithmetic, with conventional HALF_UP one-decimal presentation. Missing current R/P/L are not replaced with neutral scores. Historical-reference R5/P4 are displayed separately and are not used as current scores.

BQS=5.64→5.6; GQS=6.60→6.6. IAS known contribution=2.2100, coverage 45%, missing-weight 55%; mathematical bounds 2.7600–7.7100. These bounds are not a confidence interval or a point estimate and are not ranked.

CAP and CASH are the most judgment-sensitive factors. CAP±1 moves BQS±0.12 and GQS±0.15. CASH±1 moves BQS±0.10 and raw GQS±0.10; if subsequent evidence justifies CASH3 for persistent poor realization, final GQS is capped at 5. This is a conditional framework override, not applied to today’s CASH4. Small score differences are ties in economic interpretation.

sections.title: Business Overview
paragraphs: The company designs/processes customer-specific engineering-plastic parts, subassemblies and assemblies using thermoplastic injection, thermoset injection, compression and transfer moulding. Its output serves electrical switchgear/controls, automotive and industrial applications, with newer healthcare, childcare and precast programs. A single AS17 operating segment does not prove homogeneous customers or profitability.

Economics depend on machine loading, mould/process fit, yield, quality rejection, resin procurement, contract labor/job work, energy and customer price-reset terms. FY2026 material consumption is ₹43.1449 cr, inventory-change credit ₹2.2235 cr, job work/manpower ₹11.6111 cr, employee cost ₹3.8832 cr, electricity ₹2.5108 cr and rent ₹.8508 cr. The workforce comprises 68 employees and 215 contract workers. Contract processing grew sharply; gross material value-add is therefore not synonymous with gross profit.

The licensed additional facility increases productive access without an owned-property purchase, but lease expense and incremental deposits are real economic costs. The valuation uses post-rent EBITDA, no artificial lease-debt addition, and a separate leased-capital sensitivity in historical incremental returns. Operating property is not added again above the earnings enterprise value.

sections.title: Moat and Industry Position
paragraphs: Precision, qualification, delivery reliability and a customer-specific process/tooling fit make replacement less frictionless than buying commodity resin. Long-standing customer relationships and IATF16949/ISO9001 systems support this. The counterweight is OEM bargaining power: customer-approved raw-material sources, short orders without guaranteed long-term quantities and uncertain timing of material-price recovery.

The prospectus reports FY2023 top 5/top 10 customer concentration 58.09%/77.14% and top 10 supplier concentration 87.36%. FY2026 acknowledges concentration but provides no updated percentage. Historical concentration is not silently presented as current; no customer names or share are inferred from logos.

Primary peer reports establish a contestable industry, not an apples-to-apples valuation basket. Shaily includes regulated healthcare devices and owned IP; Mitsu emphasizes packaging/medical furniture; Time Technoplast has large industrial packaging and composites operations across geographies. Their scale, mix and competitive assets differ. No contemporaneous peer multiple is invented or transferred to Master;8 x/10 x/12 x exit assumptions are analyst sensitivity cases.

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Scale
paragraphs: Revenue grows ₹13.2528 cr in FY2021 to ₹74.3804 cr in FY2026. The preferred five-year CAGR41.20% is pandemic-base sensitive; the non-pandemic FY2023–FY2026 CAGR53.16% provides a separate cross-check. FY2020 audited revenue ₹15.0422931 cr is context, not a substituted scoring base. Operating history predates the 2023 IPO; the listing date does not truncate the business history.

The prospectus gives actual raw-material processing 23/30/40 tonnes per month against 38/40/50 capacity in FY2021/FY2022/FY2023, approximately 60.5%/75%/80% utilization. Machine clamping tonnage is not production capacity. No comparable FY2026 tonnage or selling-price bridge is disclosed, so precise unit growth and present utilization remain unknown.

FY2026 organic growth includes licensed capacity and new programs, not merger consolidation. Related-party goods sales rise from ₹.6777 cr to ₹5.6173 cr, including ₹5.4791 cr to Master Nidavellir. Removing those disclosed sales still leaves 64.80% growth in other revenue. That is evidence against a claim that all growth is circular, but it does not establish related-party collections or end-customer economics.

Two August orders disclose specific ₹3.6818597 cr and ₹.45514932 cr electrical-component work and delivery/payment terms. The former was due before cutoff; the latter by 3 November. They are not accumulated into an invented open backlog, and completion/collection is not assumed from an order announcement.

sections.title: Growth Quality and Reinvestment Runway
paragraphs: FY2023–FY2026 adjusted funding capital rises ₹12.4695 cr→₹42.239025 cr. Normalized NOPAT rises ₹1.732275 cr→₹7.88085 cr. Removing the net-tax FY2025 retrospective depreciation uplift ₹2.394675 cr from ending equity prevents a noncash accounting credit being misidentified as fresh invested capital. The resulting incremental ratio is 20.65%.

The denominator is equity plus actual gross interest-bearing debt less cash, not current ROCE masquerading as a new-capital return. It includes nonoperating assets and deposits and is therefore a conservative corporate funding proxy, not a proven project IRR. The ₹.914 cr old-depreciation proxy sensitivity and ₹4 cr lease-capital sensitivity produce 18.35% and 16.18%, respectively. Actual FY2026 depreciation under the former method is unknown.

An analyst 12–16% nominal cost-of-capital range makes these adequate to potentially attractive economics, but the evidence does not support large durable excess returns across customer cohorts. June 2026 machines, future JV funding and possible merger assets are not assigned FY2026 NOPAT before they exist in the audited perimeter.

Expansion is not free. The model charges maintenance 2.5% of sales, growth capex 20% of added annual run-rate revenue, operating deposits 0.6% of incremental revenue and 24% working capital/sales in the base. These are explicit assumptions, not engineering capacity guarantees. Higher capital intensity can eliminate financeability even when accounting earnings accelerate.

sections.title: Management, Governance and Execution
paragraphs: Promoters hold 67.10% and public holders 32.90% at 31 March 2026; public ownership is not equivalent to freely offered stock. The historical public-share count 1,316,000 is disclosed without pretending it measures executable float. No raw shareholder identity records are included in this report.

The IPO fresh issue was 700,000 shares at ₹140,₹9.8 cr gross. Net objects budget was ₹8.7416 cr, including ₹6.8166 cr working capital and ₹1.925 cr general purposes; actual FY2024 cash-flow fresh proceeds ₹8.5825 cr reflect issue costs. Offer-for-sale proceeds were not company funding. The audit reports purpose-consistent application and later narrative says full utilization; no remaining IPO cash is assumed.

Master Moulds merger terms issue 1.2 million new shares for 30,000 target shares at 40:1. Existing shares expand 30%; an unchanged old holder’s percentage falls 23.08% before options. The June 2026 NCLT direction convened meetings, not final sanction. No completed allotment appears in the dated master. Target business has real tooling operations, but revised valuation forecasts extremely high growth and margins, with approximately 84% of its operating DCF value terminal. Those assumptions are not adopted.

Master Moulds is a real operating business: FY2026 revenue ₹7.641395 cr, PAT₹2.355099 cr and CFO₹.672986 cr, with debt ₹.862979 cr and reported cash/bank ₹3.497253 cr. The latter includes ₹1.208111 cr secured FD and ₹2.201040 cr IDFCFD; interest income is not manufacturing margin. Adding target PAT without eliminations gives gross combined EPS₹18.84 versus Master ₹18.61, or ₹18.32 after the option pool. Gross combined revenue ₹82.021795 cr becomes ₹80.010795 cr after bilateral revenue elimination; intercompany profit elimination remains unknown. Potential modest accretion is real arithmetic, not a completed consolidated forecast, and no target cash, profit or synergy is prematurely credited in the base.

The FY2026 auditor resigned effective 13 August citing audit-process restructuring for amalgamation. The complete letter and regulatory annexure deny disputes, withheld information and noncooperation. Kirtane&Pandit was appointed 26 August with 22 September shareholder approval. This is a transition to monitor, not evidence of hidden fraud by itself.

Options approved 22 September cover 150,000 shares at ₹10, vesting 1–5 years; approved options are neither current shares nor received cash. The 50/50 JV initially requires ₹.05 cr from Master, while further 50% capital requirements remain uncapped. The Karnataka land dispute concerns an unsuitable 2011 allotment; the court ordered consideration of an alternative plot, not a realized cash/land award. No incremental asset value is claimed.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
paragraphs: The full main audit, CARO, IFC and audit-trail sections were reviewed, not only the headline opinion. FY2026 main and IFC opinions are unmodified, audit trail operated/preserved, and no fraud, borrowing default or statutory-dues arrears beyond six months are reported. These statements are bounded by audit scope, not guarantees of all future obligations.

CARO reports nonfiling of June/September 2025 bank returns. December stock is ₹795.05 lakh in books versus ₹1012.42 lakh to the bank, a ₹217.37 lakh/27.34% difference; March ₹904.72 lakh versus ₹1029.32 lakh,₹124.60 lakh/13.77%. The notes explicitly explain selling-price valuation for bank returns versus cost in books. That plausible basis difference is not alleged to be fraudulent book-stock overstatement; an independently reconciled/corrected series was not located.

FY2024 notes show earlier missing interim stock book values and smaller debtor/creditor differences, despite CARO’s then≤₹5 cr limit exception. The largest individual difference is ₹20.13 lakh in September debtors. March stock is ₹219.75 lakh book versus ₹211.31 lakh bank, not the erroneous OCR reading ₹222.31 lakh. FY2025 states the property-collateral facility did not require quarterly current-asset returns. Recurrence is preserved, not erased by the later explanation.

FY2025 reported earnings are distorted by ₹3.1929807 cr retrospective depreciation reversal and a separately ₹.914 cr lower annual charge. Normalized FY2025 PAT at 25% tax/no other income is ₹3.8094 cr, or ₹3.1239 cr under the old-depreciation sensitivity; FY2026 is ₹7.2678 cr. Removing the reversal from earnings but not its noncash effect from capital would distort incremental returns.

FY2024–FY2026 CFO totals ₹6.0027 cr versus PAT₹16.6122 cr, with ₹20.7285 cr cash capex. FY2026 CFO₹2.2379 cr less capex ₹5.5501 cr and deposits ₹.6098 cr gives−₹3.9220 cr before financing. FY2021–FY2023 restated CFO classifies interest as financing; later CFO includes it. Cash scoring uses the coherent later window rather than mislabeling classification as accounting error.

FY2026 receivables ₹14.8766 cr and inventory ₹9.0472 cr are partly financed by trade payables ₹5.8232 cr. Receivable days improve, but core trade working-capital intensity is essentially flat/slightly higher over the latest three years. Recent growth absorption is real, not proof that conversion will normalize. MSMED interest data, balances awaiting confirmation, GST reconciliation and unprovided leave encashment remain explicit unknowns.

Cash ₹3.0115 cr includes ₹3 cr in a current account, not an FD. ₹.9302 cr noncurrent operating deposits are invested capital, not liquid cash. Tax provision ₹2.32 cr is offset by ₹2.31 cr advance tax plus ₹.0682 cr TDS/TCS assets; the model does not charge the gross provision again. GST payable ₹.412 cr is considered alongside ₹.0548 cr ITC and ₹.001 crcash ledger. Salary/electricity provisions remain in operating working capital, not duplicated as debt-like claims. The ₹.0062 cr gratuity deficit is provided.

sections.title: Valuation and Market Expectations
paragraphs: The historical quote gives ₹157.78 cr market capitalization, reported P/E21.20 x and normalized P/E21.71 x. Using stale March cash/debt only, EV/EBITDA is 13.48 x and P/B4.29 x. These are cross-checks, not current verified net debt or intrinsic value. Post-rent earnings are used consistently; no land premium, target cash windfall or JVsynergy is added.

The explicit model bridges March 31 cash/debt to assumed October 19 entry through disclosed machine commissioning, an assumed July 29 payment of the declared FY2026 dividend, and an assumed September 30 initial JV subscription. Actual payment dates are not verified. Machine cost¥58.25 million translates to ₹3.430925 cr using the disclosed March FX rate; LC¥52.425 million corresponds to ₹3.0878325 cr. The model charges the project once and funds that amount from the disclosed machinery facility. A sensitivity allocates the otherwise unidentified 10% advance ₹.3430925 cr from creditor advances to prepaid machinery, lowers opening operating WC and June cash capex consistently.

Funding is constrained, not assumed unlimited: CC sanction ₹13 cr at 8%, annual/on-demand renewal assumed; drawing power is 75% of paid-stock proxy plus an explicitly assumed 80% eligible≤90-day receivables. Only unused sanctioned/eligible headroom is drawn. FCTL costs COFEuro+1.75%;10% is an analyst rate proxy, not the quoted 8% machinery/CCrate. Existing term principal uses ₹.8248 cr/year proxy; new machinery 60-month amortization starts atcommissioning, not after an invented grace year. LER₹1.05 cr is noncash hedging, never available liquidity.

All monthly cash uses, tax, interest, capex, working-capital build, principal and dividends are conservatively prefunded before interval EBITDA receipts. Cash floor is ₹1 cr or 2% of run-rate sales, whichever greater;₹2 cr/₹3 cr sensitivities are shown. Terminal retained cash additionally covers the next 12 months’ maintenance and any net operating/growth-capital/debt funding deficit, using full-limit CCinterest conservatively. No post-terminal cash earnings leak into exit equity.

Base 18% growth,16.5% EBITDA margin and 10 x exit produces terminal revenue ₹186.45 cr, enterprise value ₹307.65 cr, equity ₹297.99 cr and ₹718.04 per 4.15 million conditional fully diluted shares. Cash, debt, reserve, dividends and option proceeds reconcile.15% hurdle maximum ₹366.81;12%/18% alternatives ₹417.94/₹323.07. Neither entry nor exit price is guaranteed executable.

All bear/base/bull annual and dated cash rows, two-way growth/multiple and margin/WC tables, capital-intensity cases, reserve/claims/FX/nonrenewal sensitivities, dilution and execution-cost approximations are embedded in the canonical record. Reverse-growth search tests−10% through 60%, verifies finite funded brackets and residuals, and reports no solution rather than presenting an endpoint when funding fails. Faster accounting growth can worsen funding and therefore does not guarantee a higher investable return.

sections.title: Bear Case and Permanent-Loss Path
paragraphs: The critical falsifier is not one weak quoted session; it is persistent failure to turn expanded customer programs into collectible, cash-generative output. Customer loss or weaker orders reduce machine loading, while resin/contract labor costs resist adjustment. Slower collections raise eligible-collateral pressure precisely when EBITDA and bank renewal support weaken.

The bear 7% growth/12% margin/30% WC/8 x exit path first breaches the required reserve on 2027-03-31. Its going-concern terminal price ₹218.89 implies-44.51% price change but is not a funded recoverable value or an investable IRR. Ordinary IRR, conditional nonrescue return and hurdle-entry values are NULL. A separate whole-share 35%-discount/5%-fee rescue prefunds cash uses and reports dilution and return only as hypothetical unsanctioned finance.

The 28% bull expansion also becomes unfunded despite better margins, because growth investment and working capital exceed available facilities. This is a financing constraint, not proof that management has defaulted. Base renewal is an explicit assumption; the nonrenewal case repays the entire CC balance at 25 February 2027, not merely turns off further draws.

Impairment risk is High at the reference price because earnings, collections, lender support, multiple and dilution can move adversely together. Manufacturing assets and customer relationships may retain operating value, but specific liquidation recoveries, lender priority outcomes and rescue availability are not independently valued. Moderate audited leverage is important counterevidence, not immunity.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
paragraphs: Five-year 5× and 10× price outcomes require approximately 38.0% and 58.5% annual price growth, before dividends. They are not inferred from a small starting market cap. With 4.15 million terminal shares,16.5% EBITDA margin,10 x exit and optimistically zero net senior claims, required terminal revenue is roughly ₹496 cr/₹992 cr; an 8 x exit raises it further. Funding, reserves, dilution and senior claims make actual requirements more demanding.

Revenue CAGR in the table runs from 31 March 2026 to 19 October 2031, about 5.55 years, not the five-year investor-price horizon. Those arithmetic hurdles require sustained processing capacity, customer access and incremental cash investment far beyond a simple extrapolation of current machines. The disclosed domestic order amounts and a pending JV do not independently substantiate that market share or financing. The explicit high-growth five-year path already breaches its cash floor. Classification: Speculative / unsupported over five years, not an evidence-backed multibagger forecast. A longer horizon changes arithmetic but does not establish economics.

paragraphs: The following company-specific thresholds are investigation triggers, not automatic trades. Review after material financing, merger/allotment or audit events and each half-year/annual result. The research recommendation does not create a recurring reminder or task.

What would improve the thesis: sustained collected non-RPT growth, normalized cash conversion through a full capacity cycle, reconciled bank-return basis, renewed/eligible borrowing capacity and merger outcomes that demonstrably improve per-share cash earnings. Normal quote volatility alone does not falsify the business thesis.

paragraphs: Quality classification remains mixed, growth quality comparatively stronger, investment attractiveness unscoreable. Research action: watchlist and resolve implementation/funding evidence, not eligible-for-investment or buy/sell advice. The base hurdle-compatible price is conditional and cannot override a gate. An existing holder would face a different question about liquidity, concentration, taxes and exit alternatives; no holding or cost basis has been supplied.

No compounder designation: BQS, GOV, MOAT, DUR, CAP and CASH do not meet the required thresholds, even though REV is high. A price reduction would change modeled return/IAS inputs, not improve the underlying quality scores. Evidence of material diversion, unresolved unreliable assets or actual funding failure would require a different gate outcome.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions and Open Questions
paragraphs: Source priority is audited company/exchange filings, statutory annexures and dated exchange archives. Primary sources retain exact URLs, dates, locators and SHA256 metadata. Safe extracted financial facts are retained separately from original PDFs; reproduction verifies calculations from those extracts, not fresh authentication of omitted originals. All forecasts are analyst assumptions, not issuer guidance.

Open items: current physical output and utilization; customer/program margins and concentration; ≤90-day debtor eligibility; post-year cash/settlement and CC renewal; precise machine-advance allocation; MSMED interest and leave-encashment exposure; related-party collection; final merger sanction/allotment and profit elimination; option grants/exercises; capped JV commitments; complete current spreads/restrictions and no-trade classifications. No missing figure is replaced with zero.

Material reconciliations remain visible: FY2023 IPO-restated versus original financial figures; FY2024 CC debit balance classified as cash rather than negative borrowing; FY2025 policy reversal versus annual depreciation change; FY2026 bank-selling-price versus book-cost stock;₹79.8 lakh directors’ RPT remuneration versus ₹73.8 lakh P&L salary (₹6 lakh unresolved difference); target figures in ₹000 versus issuer figures in ₹lakh; NCLT meeting directions versus final sanction; gross combined revenue ₹82.021795 cr versus ₹80.010795 cr after bilateral revenue elimination. No synergies or unverified profit elimination are credited.

The supplied source register and evidence ledger distinguish disclosed facts, calculations, analyst assumptions and unknowns. Financial forecasts are fallible. This is comparative research, not a recommendation tailored to personal circumstances.

factor_audit.definition: Governance, minority protection and capital-allocation stewardship.
material_facts: Complete FY2026 main, CARO and IFC reports do not identify fraud, default, diversion or ineffective internal financial controls; the auditor resignation annexure explicitly denies information obstruction.
Bank-return failures recur across FY2024 and FY2026. The pending related-party tooling-company merger expands shares 30%, and FY2026 related-party sales are 7.55% of revenue.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: The stock valuation difference has a plausible cost-versus-selling-price explanation; a disclosed related-party transaction or auditor transition is not proof of misconduct.
factor_audit.rationale: Adequate conduct with material explainable control and allocation concerns, not a proven-abuse score. No higher stewardship rating until reconciliations and merger outcomes are evidenced.

factor_audit.definition: Contestability and durability of excess manufacturing economics.
material_facts: Customer qualification, tooling/process integration and quality systems support recurring engineering-component supply.
Historical top 10 customers account for 77.14% of revenue; customer-approved inputs and short orders limit bargaining power.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Process qualification creates friction against replacement, but competitors offer similar moulding capabilities and no unique owned IP or enduring price premium is established.
factor_audit.rationale: Useful but contestable relationships and process capability. ISO/IATF certification is a qualification standard, not by itself a structural moat.

factor_audit.definition: Demonstrated underlying revenue growth, not the size of an addressable market.
material_facts: Preferred FY2021–FY2026 revenue CAGR is 41.20%; FY2023–FY2026 cross-check is 53.16%.
Standalone operations grew organically with new licensed capacity. Excluding disclosed related-party goods sales, FY2026 revenue still grew 64.80%.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: FY2021 is a pandemic-affected base; actual production, selling-price and customer-program growth splits are unavailable. Related-party revenue increased substantially.
factor_audit.rationale: Reported CAGR earns raw 9, reduced only by the Medium-confidence ceiling of 8. No size/order-book bonus or discretionary modifier; economic capacity and recurring EBITDA corroborate substantial real growth.

factor_audit.definition: Accessible demand and reinvestment runway, excluding capital-return quality.
material_facts: Electrical controls, industrial, automotive and emerging healthcare/childcare/precast programs offer several accessible end markets.
Seven commissioned machines in June 2026 and dated electrical-component orders demonstrate capacity and customer access beyond a generic TAM.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Current concentration, committed long-term quantities, new-machine utilization and program margins are not quantified; recurring OEM orders are not an irrevocable backlog.
factor_audit.rationale: A credible expansion runway exists, but customer dependence, procurement cycles and unseasoned capacity constrain durability confidence.

factor_audit.definition: Attributable incremental NOPAT relative to additional invested capital.
material_facts: FY2023–FY2026 adjusted corporate capital increases ₹29.7695 cr while normalized NOPAT increases ₹6.1486 cr:20.65% incremental return.
A₹.914 cr annual old-depreciation proxy lowers the estimate to 18.35%; adding ₹4 cr lease-capital sensitivity lowers it further to 16.18%, against an analyst 12–16% cost-of-capital range.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: No plant/customer cohort attribution is disclosed, rental capacity makes capital comparability imperfect, and June 2026 assets have not produced FY2026 audited earnings.
factor_audit.rationale: Adequate, potentially attractive incremental economics, not proven durable large excess returns. The bridge supports scoring rather than requiring unavailable private cohorts, while uncertainty prevents 7–8.

factor_audit.definition: Operating cash realization and working-capital discipline.
material_facts: FY2024–FY2026 CFO/PAT is 0.3613 x, or 0.4222 x after removing the FY2025 depreciation reversal at 25% tax; cash capex exceeds CFO in each year.
Core trade working capital/sales is 23.44%,24.32%,24.34% in FY2024–FY2026, not a recent declining intensity; FY2026 deposits absorb a further ₹.6098 cr.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: CFO remains positive; FY2026 receivable days improve to 73 and 98.99% of receivables are under six months. Real growth explains some absorption but does not establish full collection or prove the weakness transient.
factor_audit.rationale: Weak realized conversion merits 4. Persistent poor cash realization alone can justify≤3 under the framework. Here positive cash generation, predominantly young receivables and evidenced growth absorption support a borderline 4 rather than 3; this is a judgment, not proof that weakness is temporary. Monitoring remains demanding.

factor_audit.definition: Funding resilience, claims and access to liquidity.
material_facts: FY2026 gross debt ₹10.859 cr, cash ₹3.0115 cr and net debt/EBITDA0.64 x are manageable on audited earnings.

Disclosed facilities include ₹13 cr CC and ₹3.15 cr machinery finance. The conservative base waterfall funds essential uses without equity rescue under explicit renewal and eligible-collateral assumptions.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: CC is on-demand/12-month, only≤90-day receivables and paid stock qualify, Euro debt floats, and linked bear/high-growth cases breach the cash floor.
factor_audit.rationale: Manageable base case with meaningful stress sensitivity. Neither the aggregate ₹22.10 cr facility nor all stated cash is treated as unconditional spare liquidity.

factor_audit.definition: Delivery of operating commitments and adaptation.
material_facts: FY2024–FY2026 revenue expands ₹25.29 cr to ₹74.38 cr and recurring EBITDA₹4.28 cr to ₹12.29 cr, corroborating delivered scaling rather than only announcements.
June 2026 machinery commissioning is disclosed with models and cost; IPO working-capital use is reported as deployed.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Current machine utilization, program-level returns and order completion cash receipts are unavailable; merger and JV milestones remain incomplete at the cutoff.
factor_audit.rationale: Demonstrated expansion with incomplete milestone-to-cash evidence. Not enough repeated, fully measured execution cycles for a high score.

factor_audit.definition: Recurring operating sources of profit growth and per-share outcomes.
material_facts: FY2026 normalized PAT excluding other income at 25% tax is ₹7.2678 cr, versus ₹3.8094 cr for FY2025; EBITDA margins 15.32%→16.52% support recurring operating improvement.
FY2025 reported PAT includes a ₹3.193 cr retrospective depreciation reversal; current depreciation also falls ₹.914 cr versus the previous method.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: FY2026 normalized earnings growth is real, but approved options and the pending share-swap can dilute per-share claims; target-company FD income must not become a manufacturing margin.
factor_audit.rationale: Mixed comparability and prospective dilution prevent a high earnings-quality score despite strong normalized operating progress.

factor_audit.definition: Supported base-case annualized return relative to the 15% nominal pretax equity hurdle.
material_facts: The base case at the 16 October historical ₹394.45 quote produces 13.32% dated five-year IRR under stated funding assumptions.
The resulting spread is-1.68 percentage points; the framework−2 to<0 band is 5.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: The quote is historical, execution costs are not observed and funding depends on renewals/collateral eligibility. Bear and bull paths with cash-floor breaches have no ordinary IRR.
factor_audit.rationale: Current-price factor NS because no authenticated cutoff-session quote. Historical-reference scenario assessment follows: Mechanically derived from the supported conditional base model, not an additional qualitative haircut.

factor_audit.definition: Downside severity and survival under linked operating and financing stress.
material_facts: The bear case combines 7% growth,12% EBITDA margin,30% working capital/sales and 8 x exit; its first cash-floor breach is 2027-03-31.
Full CC nonrenewal repayment on 25 February 2027 also breaches the funding floor. Hypothetical rescue is separately priced at 35% discount plus 5% fees.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Audited leverage is moderate, cash generation remains positive and sanctioned facilities support the base case; modeled cash-floor breaches are not evidence of an actual default.
factor_audit.rationale: Material impairment and recapitalization risk under credible linked stress. Terminal prices on unfunded paths are illustrations, not reliable realizable recoveries.

factor_audit.definition: Demandingness and robustness of price-implied assumptions.
material_facts: Base 18% growth,16.5% EBITDA margin and 10 x exit do not reach the 15% hurdle at ₹394.45; the conditional 15% maximum price is ₹366.81.
A12% hurdle has a funded reverse-growth root, while 15% and 18% have no funded crossing in the tested growth range at unchanged base margin/capital intensity.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: The base growth is far below recent history, but extrapolating historical growth requires more working capital and capex; it is not a free valuation cure.
factor_audit.rationale: Current-price factor NS because no authenticated cutoff-session quote. Historical-reference scenario assessment follows: Limited room for execution, funding or multiple errors. Separate from R: this factor assesses assumption robustness rather than return level alone.

factor_audit.definition: Practical execution and exit for the illustrative ₹500,000 reference position.
material_facts: Only 43 issuer rows appear in 60 validated exchange-session archives and 15 in 20; missing rows cannot be declared zero-trade sessions.
The current lot is 500 shares. Observed median 1500 shares/day gives zero whole-lot capacity at 2%,5% or 10% participation.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Actual trading exists, including 1000 shares on 16 October, but spreads, complete surveillance status and the full-window no-trade denominator are not verified.
factor_audit.confidence: Low for execution; High for retained historical rows
factor_audit.rationale: NS, not an invented low or neutral point score. G4 holds new-purchase implementation; IAS remains incomplete.

summary: Master Components is a genuine small engineering-plastics manufacturer with rapid organic scaling, not merely an announced capacity story. Recurring EBITDA has grown with sales, and an adjusted three-year capital bridge suggests adequate incremental returns. Those strengths coexist with weak earnings-to-cash realization, customer bargaining power, recurring bank-reporting weaknesses and unsettled dilution.
